what_its_for: Guselkumab is used to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (a skin condition causing red, scaly patches) in adults. It is also used to treat psoriatic arthritis (a type of arthritis that affects people with psoriasis). It works by blocking a protein in your immune system called IL-23 that causes inflammation.
how_to_take: Guselkumab is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection). It comes in a prefilled syringe or a One-Press injector pen. You can inject it yourself at home after your doctor or nurse shows you how to do it properly. Common injection sites include the stomach area (abdomen), thighs, or upper arms. Rotate your injection sites each time and avoid skin that is bruised, tender, red, or affected by psoriasis. Let the pen or syringe sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before injecting — do not try to warm it in a microwave or hot water.
dosing: For plaque psoriasis: You will receive 100 mg injected under the skin at Week 0, Week 4, and then once every 8 weeks (every 2 months) after that. For psoriatic arthritis: Your doctor will determine your dosing schedule, which may involve injections every 4 weeks or every 8 weeks. Always follow the schedule your doctor gives you. It helps to mark your injection dates on a calendar so you do not miss a dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember. Then continue your regular dosing schedule from that point. Do not inject two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Store guselkumab in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it — if it accidentally freezes, do not use it. Do not shake the pen or syringe. If needed, you can store it at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) for up to 8 hours, but once removed from the refrigerator, do not put it back. Keep it out of reach of children. Dispose of used pens or syringes in an approved sharps container — never throw them in the regular trash.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting live vaccines (such as the nasal flu vaccine, shingles live vaccine, or yellow fever vaccine) while using guselkumab, as it may make these vaccines less safe or effective. Talk to your doctor before getting any vaccines. Tell your doctor if you have any signs of infection before starting or during treatment. Avoid being around people who are sick, and wash your hands regularly to reduce your risk of infection.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: signs of serious infection such as fever, chills, cough, shortness of breath, burning with urination, or painful skin sores; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness; any new or worsening health problems. Also let your doctor know before starting treatment if you have any infections, tuberculosis (TB) or have been around someone with TB, liver problems, or if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
when_it_works: Many people start to see improvement in their skin within 4 weeks, but it may take up to 16 weeks or longer to see the full benefit. For psoriatic arthritis, improvement in joint symptoms may also take several weeks. Be patient and keep using the medication as directed, even if you do not see results right away. Do not stop using it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not fully known if guselkumab is safe to use during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Older adults (65 and over): Guselkumab can be used in older adults, but older patients may have a slightly higher risk of infection. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Children: Guselkumab is not currently approved for use in children under 18 years of age. Infections or weakened immune system: Tell your doctor if you have a history of frequent infections or a condition that affects your immune system, as guselkumab lowers your immune response.
